claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 19 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 19 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand a bit about your situation.

**First, let me ask about your child:**

1. **What is your child's name?** (I'll need this to keep track if you have multiple children)

2. **How old is your child?** This is important because eligibility rules differ based on age:
   - Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
   - Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
   - Children aged 20 or over don't qualify

Please share your child's name and age, and we'll work through their eligibility together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. My child's name is Alex, and they're 19 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So we're assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 19 years old**.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19 years old, they may still qualify for Child Benefit, but this depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

Let me check the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In approved education or training?** (such as full-time non-advanced education, or approved training programs)

2. **Has Alex recently left education or training?** (within the last few months)

3. **Neither** - not currently in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - they're doing their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form college, they are in education. Now I need to check that the education meets the requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! A-levels are specifically listed as **approved non-advanced education** for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to verify a few more details about Alex's education:

**1. Is this full-time education?** (At least 12 hours per week of supervised study - this includes classroom time, lectures, and supervised workshops. A-levels at sixth form college are typically full-time, so this should be fine)

**2. Is this education funded by an employer, or is there an agreement for a future job with an employer?** (This would typically not apply to standard sixth form A-levels)

Can you confirm these details about Alex's A-level course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's full-time - Alex is there every weekday during term time. And no, there's no employer involved - it's just the regular sixth form college course.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what we need. A-levels at sixth form college on a full-time basis with no employer involvement definitely qualifies as approved education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not working at all)?**

Children aged 16 or over who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit, even if they're also in education. However, part-time work (under 24 hours per week) is fine.

Does Alex work, and if so, is it less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're just focused on their studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's completely fine. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question about Alex:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?** 

Specifically, children who receive Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own name are not eligible for Child Benefit. 

Does Alex receive any of these benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship?**

The rules vary by region:
- **English apprenticeships** (all types) would disqualify from Child Benefit
- **Scottish Modern Apprenticeships** would disqualify
- **Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships** are approved
- **Other Welsh apprenticeships** would disqualify

Since you mentioned Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form college, I assume they're NOT doing an apprenticeship - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship, just the regular A-level course.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now we've established that Alex qualifies as an eligible child. The next step is to check **your eligibility as the claimant**.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check **your residency status** as the claimant:

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You'll qualify if **ANY** of these apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are:
   - Working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3+ months), OR
   - Actively seeking work (up to 91 days), OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and family (not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit), OR
   - Studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - Are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
4. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Living normally in the UK meets the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. You'll qualify if **ANY** of these apply:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide (in money or equivalent value through food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds Child Benefit

Which situation applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Living with Alex clearly establishes your responsibility. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Someone else who cares for Alex

This is important because only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree on who should be the claimant.

Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following best describes where Alex is living?**

1. **In hospital** (currently an inpatient)
2. **In care** (placed in local authority care or residential care home)
3. **Fostered** (living with foster carers)
4. **Living normally at home** with you

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is contributing financially towards the child's care.

Is the council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me get the final outcome for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
# 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex. Here's why:

✅ **Alex qualifies as an eligible child** because they are:
- 19 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels)
- Studying at least 12 hours per week in supervised education
- Not working 24+ hours per week
- Not receiving benefits in their own right
- Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

✅ **You qualify as an eligible claimant** because you:
- Normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- Live with Alex and are responsible for them
- Are the only person claiming for Alex
- Have no local council contributions towards Alex's care

---

## **Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
   - Online: Visit https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   
2. **Prepare these documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important note about the High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay a tax charge
   - You can still claim and choose not to receive payments but maintain your National Insurance credits

4. **Payment details:**
   - Paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

**Need help with your application?** Visit the official government website at https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim for full guidance.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?
